title: Agent verbs
description: The tracker-neutral ost verbs agents call, as commands and as runtime tools.
---

<!-- Generated by `pnpm --filter @outstaff/agent run docs:verbs`. Do not edit by hand. -->

Agents never talk to the tracker, the knowledge base or the code host directly. They call these verbs, which work the same whatever adapters the team uses. Every verb is available two ways from one library: as a command (`ost ticket show ACME-12`) and as an in-process runtime tool (`ticket_show`).

- Every result carries the URLs of the things it touches, built from the adapters' link templates.
- Inputs are validated; there are no destructive verbs (nothing deletes, force-merges or edits other people's text).
- `pr resolve` goes through the code host adapter, which refuses unless the last comment in the thread is yours.
- A verb that needs a port the team has not configured fails with `unsupported` ("no tracker configured for this team"); the office verbs (`ask`, `work`, `roster`) fail with `unavailable` when the agent is not connected to an office.
- Commands take `--json` to print `{ text, data, links }`; errors print `{ error: { code, message } }`. The identity comes from `OUTSTAFF_PERSON` and the team from `--team` or the usual team lookup.

## ticket.show

Show a ticket with its description and comments.

Shows a ticket: title, status, assignee, labels, description and its comments, with the ticket URL.

```
ost ticket show <key>
```

Runtime tool: `ticket_show`

| Input | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | string | yes | Ticket key, for example ACME-12. |

Examples:

```sh
ost ticket show ACME-12
```

## ticket.comment

Add a comment to a ticket.

Adds a comment to a ticket and returns the link to it.

```
ost ticket comment <key> <body>
```

Runtime tool: `ticket_comment`

| Input | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | string | yes | Ticket key, for example ACME-12. |
| `body` | string | yes | Comment text, Markdown. |

Examples:

```sh
ost ticket comment ACME-12 "Pull request is up for review."
```

## ticket.move

Move a ticket to another status.

Moves a ticket to a canonical status (backlog, ready, active, review, blocked, done, canceled). The tracker's own status names are mapped by the team's workflow settings.

```
ost ticket move <key> <to>
```

Runtime tool: `ticket_move`

| Input | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | string | yes | Ticket key, for example ACME-12. |
| `to` | backlog \| ready \| active \| review \| blocked \| done \| canceled | yes | Canonical status to move to. |

Examples:

```sh
ost ticket move ACME-12 review
```

## ticket.assign

Assign a ticket to a member, to yourself or to nobody.

Assigns a ticket. "to" is a tracker member (username, name or id), "me" for yourself, or "none" to unassign.

```
ost ticket assign <key> <to>
```

Runtime tool: `ticket_assign`

| Input | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | string | yes | Ticket key, for example ACME-12. |
| `to` | string | yes | Member username, name or id; "me"; or "none". |

Examples:

```sh
ost ticket assign ACME-12 me
ost ticket assign ACME-12 none
```

## doc.search

Search the knowledge base.

Searches documents by text and lists the matches with their URLs.

```
ost doc search <query> [--limit <limit>]
```

Runtime tool: `doc_search`

| Input | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `query` | string | yes | Words to search for. |
| `limit` | integer | no | Maximum number of results. Default: 10. |

Examples:

```sh
ost doc search "checkout flow"
```

## doc.show

Show a document and its comments.

Shows a document's text and its comment threads, with ids you can reply to or resolve.

```
ost doc show <id>
```

Runtime tool: `doc_show`

| Input | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | yes | Document id or path. |

Examples:

```sh
ost doc show specs/checkout.md
```

## doc.create

Create a document.

Creates a new document. It never overwrites: an existing path is a conflict.

```
ost doc create <path> --title <title> --body <body>
```

Runtime tool: `doc_create`

| Input | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string | yes | Path of the document in the knowledge base, for example specs/checkout.md. |
| `title` | string | yes | Document title. |
| `body` | string | yes | Document text, Markdown. |

Examples:

```sh
ost doc create specs/checkout.md --title "Checkout" --body "# Checkout"
```

## doc.reply

Reply to a comment on a document.

Replies to a comment thread on a document.

```
ost doc reply <doc> <commentId> <body>
```

Runtime tool: `doc_reply`

| Input | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `doc` | string | yes | Document id or path. |
| `commentId` | string | yes | Comment id. |
| `body` | string | yes | Reply text, Markdown. |

Examples:

```sh
ost doc reply specs/checkout.md c-3 "Done, see the new section."
```

## doc.resolve

Resolve a comment thread on a document.

Marks a comment thread on a document as resolved.

```
ost doc resolve <doc> <commentId>
```

Runtime tool: `doc_resolve`

| Input | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `doc` | string | yes | Document id or path. |
| `commentId` | string | yes | Comment id. |

Examples:

```sh
ost doc resolve specs/checkout.md c-3
```

## pr.status

Show a pull request's state, checks and open review threads.

Shows a pull request: state, mergeability, checks and how many review threads are still open, with URLs.

```
ost pr status <repo> <number>
```

Runtime tool: `pr_status`

| Input | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `repo` | string | yes | Repository: its name in team.yaml (for example shop) or host/owner/name. |
| `number` | integer | yes | Pull request number. |

Examples:

```sh
ost pr status shop 42
```

## pr.threads

List the review threads of a pull request.

Lists the review threads of a pull request with their ids, locations, comments and URLs. Open threads only unless all is set.

```
ost pr threads <repo> <number> [--all]
```

Runtime tool: `pr_threads`

| Input | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `repo` | string | yes | Repository: its name in team.yaml (for example shop) or host/owner/name. |
| `number` | integer | yes | Pull request number. |
| `all` | boolean | no | Include resolved threads. Default: false. |

Examples:

```sh
ost pr threads shop 42
ost pr threads shop 42 --all
```

## pr.resolve

Resolve a review thread whose last comment is yours.

Resolves a review thread after you have replied. It refuses when the last comment in the thread is not yours; the reviewer resolves those.

```
ost pr resolve <repo> <number> <thread>
```

Runtime tool: `pr_resolve`

| Input | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `repo` | string | yes | Repository: its name in team.yaml (for example shop) or host/owner/name. |
| `number` | integer | yes | Pull request number. |
| `thread` | string | yes | Thread id from pr threads. |

Examples:

```sh
ost pr resolve shop 42 PRT_abc123
```

## me

Show who you are on this team.

Shows your handle, role, repository grants and which integrations this team has connected.

```
ost me
```

Runtime tool: `me`

Examples:

```sh
ost me
```

## ask

Ask a teammate a question through the office.

Asks another person of the team a question. The office routes it; the answer may come later, as a new message in your work item.

```
ost ask <to> <question>
```

Runtime tool: `ask`

| Input | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `to` | string | yes | Handle of the teammate. |
| `question` | string | yes | The question, with enough context to answer it. |

Examples:

```sh
ost ask mira "Should the cart survive a deploy?"
```

## work

List your work items.

Lists the work items the office has scheduled for you, with their tickets and pull requests.

```
ost work
```

Runtime tool: `work`

Examples:

```sh
ost work
```

## team

List the team and what everyone is doing.

Lists the people of the team with their roles and current status.

```
ost roster
```

Runtime tool: `team`

Examples:

```sh
ost roster
```
